order_note: No predecessor: SQL 147 creates one new SECURITY DEFINER function, aws_record_external_disbursement(uuid, uuid, jsonb, text), on the disbursement, check, transfer and stakeholder schema the AWS databases already have (disbursement_batches with id, tenant_id, check_intake_item_id, created_by, check_amount, available_amount, reserve_held, status, notes, completed_at, approved_at, approved_by and approved_amount_cents; disbursement_splits with id, batch_id, tenant_id, amount, status, method, external_check_number, recipient_name, recipient_type, external_notes, stakeholder_account_id, idempotence_key and settled_at; check_intake_items with id, tenant_id, amount, pa_fee_pct and pa_fee_amount; payment_transfers with tenant_id, check_id, leg_role, status and amount_cents; stakeholder_accounts with id, tenant_id and nickname; check_stakeholders with check_intake_item_id, tenant_id and stakeholder_account_id), SQL 90's aws_can_write_tenant(uuid) (SQL 90 applied in production), auth.uid() and role checksops; a read-only production inspect confirms them. The applying login must reach all six relations as the function's owner past RLS (definer_can_write_relations: the table owner without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, or a superuser or BYPASSRLS): a DEFINER filtered by RLS would under-count what was already paid. Expected pre-state in both environments: the function absent (release sql147 v1, derived: a60b06089007f083007ac7b24ae41cdd1cd33b0cbd04c63985c09faa9b666286). Where it already exists (a re-run) it must be owned by the applying login (functions_owned_by_login), keep its jsonb result (function_results_match) and hold no EXECUTE grant other than checksops and the owner, which the file keeps, and PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role, which it revokes (function_acl_replaceable). The ACL after the apply is checksops and the owner. The API change that calls it (aws/functions/api/external-disbursement.mjs, overlay member external-disbursement.mjs with sql_before SQL 147) needs the guarded Lambda path after this pin is applied in that environment; until then recording an external payment fails, as today. No API, Lambda or SPA change is part of this pin. Adds no trigger.

intended_post_state.note: aws_record_external_disbursement(uuid, uuid, jsonb, text), owned by checksops_admin, plpgsql, VOLATILE, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path public, pg_temp, RETURNS jsonb, EXECUTE for checksops and the owner (PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role revoked). Only for a signed-in member of the tenant (auth.uid() and aws_can_write_tenant(_tenant_id); 42501 external_disbursement_forbidden); inputs checked (22023 external_disbursement_invalid: an idempotency key of 8-100 characters, 1-10 payments, whole-cent amounts > 0, a recipient name or a stakeholder account of the tenant or of its check_stakeholders row for this check, the Funds tab's recipient types, length limits); the check locked FOR UPDATE and owned by the tenant (P0002 external_disbursement_check_not_found); the same key returns the recorded batch (duplicate true) and other payments under it are 23505 external_disbursement_key_reused; a total above the amount available (check amount - PA fee - the tenant's live splits and Moov send legs on the check) is P0001 external_disbursement_exceeds_available; otherwise one completed disbursement_batches row and one settled external_check disbursement_splits row per payee. No other function, table, column, policy, RLS setting, grant, trigger or row change; no payment_transfers row. The fingerprint is releaseIntendedHash('sql147', file bytes) (scripts/deployment-guard/lib/release-sql-state.mjs): 8080fbd7c4c24ed07251584b47b6507b0ee07095645c73c3cded7f12f3acd499.
